Bimetallic Thermometer Diagram Explained Label by Label

Bimetallic thermometer diagram drawings show a round dial on top of a long stem, with a coiled bimetal helix at the bottom of the stem joined to the pointer by a thin shaft. When you read a bimetallic thermometer diagram, trace it from the hot stem tip upward to the dial, because that is the path the signal follows.

Label in the diagramLocationWhat it does
PointerFront of the dialShows the temperature on the scale
Dial and scaleInside the sealed casePrinted range in °C or °F
Case and windowTop of the gaugeProtects the dial, may hold silicone fill
Connection fittingBetween case and stemThreaded, union or flange joint to the thermowell
StemBelow the fittingStainless tube that carries heat to the sensing element
Central shaftAlong the stem axisTransfers helix rotation to the pointer without gears
Bimetal helixBottom of the stemTwists as temperature changes; the sensitive part
Fixed endStem tipAnchors the lower end of the helix

How to Sketch One in an Exam

  1. Draw a circle for the dial with a pointer at the centre.
  2. Draw a long narrow rectangle below it for the stem.
  3. Draw a coil near the bottom of the stem and label it bimetal helix.
  4. Join the top of the coil to the pointer with a straight line marked shaft.
  5. Mark the fixed lower end and show the twist direction with an arrow.
